issue.title: Rotate the obsidian-headless sync.log; it is 1.0 GB and append-only
issue.description:
`~/.config/obsidian-headless/sync/8a259ad922718b6d8400c1f0e3ba8abe/sync.log` is
append-only and has no rotation. It was 982 MB when epic bob-cli-1e phase
bob-cli-1e.5 first measured it on 2026-08-27 and 1.0 GB two hours later, while
the vault it logs for is only 114.5 MB.

`ob-sync-bob.service` runs `~/.local/bin/ob-sync-bob-poll`, which invokes
`ob sync --path /home/bryan/bob` every 30 seconds. The poll script itself never
opens sync.log (`grep -c 'sync.log' ~/.local/bin/ob-sync-bob-poll` is 0);
obsidian-headless writes it from inside its own per-vault config directory, so
the fix belongs in a logrotate/systemd-timer rule or a truncation step around
the poll loop, not in the `ob` client.

The current `Vault limit exceeded` outage makes it worse: every 30-second cycle
now appends a full failure stack trace.

Proposed by bob-cli-1e.5 (epic bob-cli-1e, Remove old_lib from Obsidian Sync and
restore the vault under quota) as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1.

task_type_fields.impact: Consumes unbounded disk on athena (already 1.0 GB for a 114.5 MB vault) and makes the log unreadable without tail; growth accelerates during any sync outage because each failed 30s cycle appends a stack trace.
task_type_fields.repro:
```bash
ls -l ~/.config/obsidian-headless/sync/8a259ad922718b6d8400c1f0e3ba8abe/sync.log
# 2026-08-27 09:05 -> 1.0 GB, still growing every 30s
systemctl --user status ob-sync-bob.service   # confirms the 30s poll loop is live
```
